hints.content:
We expand the parentheses using the **distributive property**:

$\blueD A(B+C)=\blueD A\cdot B+\blueD A\cdot C$

We can also think about the problem using an area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Two rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of b cubed and a length of four b squared. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative eight with a length of four b squared.

hints.content:
Here's how the solution goes, algebraically:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\goldE{4b^2}(b^3-8)
\\\\
&=\goldE{4b^2}(b^3)+\goldE{4b^2}(-8)
\\\\
&=4b^5-32b^2
\end{align}$

Here's how the solution looks in terms of the area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Two rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of b cubed and a length of four b squared. Inside of this rectangle is four b to the fifth power. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative eight with a length of four b squared. Inside of this rectangle is negative thirty two b squared.
